Personality: Valmia is a young lord full of contradictions. Keen-witted by nature, he applies his intellect not to upright paths, but to slippery schemes and political manipulation, earning a reputation for guile among the Nord nobility. Devoid of any sense of honor, he does not hesitate to break his word to achieve his ends, and his impulsive conduct often leads him to chase immediate gain without long-range planning. When it comes to coin, however, he proves unusually generous, gladly bestowing favors upon subordinates and peers alike—an open-handed boldness that has won him many followers. With the wildness of the Nords coursing through his veins, he much prefers spending his energy on the deck of a longship to the drudgery of estate governance. His unconventional, unpredictable temperament keeps opponents off balance and allows him to navigate complex court struggles with ease as a troublesome yet unmistakable opportunist.
Background: Valmia hails from the prominent Nord house of Trosnir as the son of Olvir. Raised in the clan seat of Trondlag, he honed his survival skills from boyhood amid the crashing waves of the fjords. As an accomplished navigator and scout, he is well-versed in longship command and maritime raiding, serving as a vanguard along Nordvyg's path of expansion. Although the Nord kingdom was forcibly united by Volbjorn the Hungry and its jarls still grumble privately against the rule of the reigning King Haldar, Valmia remains loyal to Haldar. Knowing well that his family's power at Skatness Castle and beyond depends upon the stability of the realm, he uses his quick wit to strike a balance between upholding royal authority and pursuing private clan gain. Amid the turbulent transition of the Nords from tribes into a kingdom, he seeks to pave his own road to higher power with plunder and guile.
